body:
#59825 made the association scope unable to remove the key condition when loading the association, but removing it on purpose is a common pattern, as pointed out in https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/59825#issuecomment-6944500296:

```ruby
class User < ActiveRecord::Base
  has_many :messages, ->(user) {
    unscope(where: :user_id).where("sender_id = :id OR recipient_id = :id", id: user.id)
  }
end
```

With the key added back, such an association silently returns other records, or none, when the key column exists. The polymorphic type condition of an `as:` association could also be removed or replaced by the association scope in every path, so the association loaded records it doesn't write.

Put both behind `config.active_record.association_scope_keeps_owner_conditions`, enabled by `load_defaults "8.2"`. When disabled, the association scope can still remove or replace them, with a deprecation warning. In Rails 9.0 they will always be applied.
title: Add `association_scope_keeps_owner_conditions` to keep the owner conditions of associations
